summary: Playing Wingspan feels like a calm, puzzly engine-builder where you chain bird powers across three habitat rows to snowball food, eggs, and card draws, then cash in on end-round and end-game bonus cards. Turns are quick and mostly solitaire-ish, with occasional envy when someone else's bird power triggers off your dice roll.
praised: Gorgeous, high-quality bird art and components
Satisfying engine-building as bird combos click together
Approachable rules with real depth in play
Broad appeal, including to non-gamers and birders
criticised: Low direct interaction, can feel multiplayer solitaire
Heavy luck of the draw in which bird cards/bonus cards you get
Bird powers vary widely in strength, leading to snowballing
End-game/round bonus cards can feel like hidden scoring races

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with occasional food/tray competition

scoring.why: Points come from bird card values, eggs, cached food, tucked cards, and bonus/round-goal cards, so the winner is usually whoever best combines several of these sources rather than maxing one.
